🧠 Crypto News Brief: Self-custody took the hardest hit of the year as a five-year-old firmware flaw emptied hundreds of Coldcard wallets. Meanwhile, earnings season laid bare how deeply the Q2 drawdown cut into crypto's biggest balance sheets. 🔓 Coldcard Firmware Flaw Drains 594 BTC in a 25-Minute Sweep An attacker emptied roughly 500 single-signature Bitcoin wallets between 01:31 and 01:56 UTC, moving about 594 BTC — some $38 million — across 500 transactions inside a three-block window, then consolidating 562 BTC into a single address that has not moved since. Block's Bitcoin engineering team traced the cause to Coldcard firmware that had silently bypassed its dedicated hardware random number generator since March 2021, producing seeds weak enough to be guessed. Every drained wallet was created inside that window. Coinkite has shipped emergency patches and is urging affected holders to migrate funds. Read full story ⚖️ New York Sues Kalshi, Calling Prediction Markets "Gambling, Plain and Simple" Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James filed suit in Manhattan state court alleging KalshiEX runs an unlicensed gambling business, seeking an injunction, forfeiture of profits, restitution for users and fines equal to three times the company's gains — exposure the state estimates could reach $36 billion. Kalshi dismissed the action as political theater, arguing states cannot shut down a federally licensed exchange. The CFTC has filed for a temporary restraining order to halt New York's case. More details 📉 Strategy Books $8.2 Billion Quarterly Loss on Bitcoin Markdown Michael Saylor's Strategy reported an $8.22 billion second-quarter net loss, driven almost entirely by an $8.32 billion unrealized markdown under fair-value accounting after bitcoin fell roughly 14% during the quarter. The firm holds 843,775 BTC worth about $54.8 billion against a $63.7 billion cost basis. It has built a $3.75 billion dollar reserve — enough to cover preferred dividends and interest for more than two years — and has started selling small tranches of bitcoin to fund them, a clear break from its buy-and-hold doctrine. Most companies have an architecture problem.  OpenAI just reset the
 economics of AI agents;  Why AI Tools Break at Enterprise Scale...
76767.body:
AI Frontier

Автор: Steve Nouri


Автор: Steve Nouri

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/most-companies-have-architecture-problem-openai-just-reset-nouri-r8jfc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BGnPthqTUQEy0GoQ7E0OGJA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=33szPU6IRE5co1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~ms94s5im~qm-null-null&eid=fz96fz-ms94s5im-qm
  
OpenAI has cut GPT-5.6 Luna’s API price by 80% and Terra’s by 20%. Luna now costs just $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens, while Terra comes in at $2 and $12. Sol pricing remains unchanged. But this is bigger than another model price cut. OpenAI is making capable, tool-using intelligence cheap enough to run continuously in the background not just when a user opens a chatbot. Those optimizations reportedly: → Reduced end-to-end serving costs by 20% → Improved token-generation efficiency by more than 15% → Created enough savings for OpenAI to pass some of the gains to customers OpenAI also introduced Fast mode for Sol, delivering up to 2.5× faster performance than standard processing at twice the price, without changing the model’s intelligence. The important number is no longer cost per token. It is cost per successful outcome. A cheap model that repeatedly fails, retries tools, generates excessive tokens, or requires a more capable model to correct its work may ultimately be more expensive. GPT-5.6’s three-tier structure points toward a different architecture: Sol decides. Use it for planning, ambiguity, complex judgment, and high-stakes decisions. Terra operates. Use it for everyday knowledge work where capability, speed, and reliability must remain balanced. Luna executes at scale. Use it for well-defined coding tasks, classification, extraction, testing, monitoring, and background agent loops. The deeper shift This announcement reveals a potentially powerful flywheel: More capable AI helps engineers optimize AI infrastructure. Better infrastructure lowers inference costs. Lower prices generate more usage. More usage creates more opportunities to improve models and systems. The model is no longer only the product. It is becoming part of the machinery used to improve and operate the product. Why it matters This price drop could unlock a wave of AI products that were previously uneconomical: → Agents monitoring systems around the clock → Continuous document and inbox processing → Thousands of parallel coding and testing tasks → AI embedded inside every operational workflow → Personalized services running persistently for every customer No funding yet?
